title: Telecom complaint and service credit assistant
brief: Design a complaint assistant for a telecom provider. Customers report network outages, poor speed and billing errors. The assistant should investigate using account, billing and service records, explain findings and resolve eligible service credits. Larger or unclear refunds need a human supervisor and may wait up to 48 hours. Keep customers informed, avoid duplicate refunds and use only the right customer's active service connection. Propose any missing policies as assumptions, not real company rules.

assumptions.statement: Proposed pilot policy P1: verified outage credits equal floor(monthly recurring service charge in minor units × verified outage seconds / billing-period seconds), capped at the remaining recurring charge. Auto cap is 1000 minor units INR per incident; poor speed without a verified service breach and billing errors require supervisor review.
assumptions.why: A safe narrow first release needs an explicit rule.
assumptions.validation: Approve currency, tax, rounding, eligibility, caps, overlapping incidents and legal treatment.

assumptions.statement: Account, service and billing adapters must offer authenticated tenant/subject reads, active connection version checks, scoped credit posting with a unique business-event key and definitive operation readback.
assumptions.why: Unknown provider capabilities block safe writes.
assumptions.validation: Sandbox contract tests prove atomic duplicate exclusion, commit proof and readback; otherwise assist-only.

assumptions.statement: Proposed supervisor queue is staffed continuously, acknowledges cases within 1 elapsed hour, decides within 48 elapsed hours, and a duty manager owns overdue cases. Portal updates appear on entry and at 24 hours; overdue notice appears at 48 hours.
assumptions.why: 48-hour wait requires a real owner and clock.
assumptions.validation: Staffing, portal access, event schemas and durable scheduler sign-off.

assumptions.statement: Proposed retention is 30 days for redacted model traces and 365 days for financial audit; deployment region, deletion exceptions and customer permissions need privacy review.
assumptions.why: No jurisdiction or retention rules supplied.
assumptions.validation: Approve data map, roles, residency and retention before real customer data.

assumptions.statement: Illustrative traffic is 10000 cases/month; one explanation call per case, maximum two attempts. Assume 10% retry rate and 2000 input/300 output tokens at $1/$4 per million tokens.
assumptions.why: Budget only; no provider selected or measured usage.
assumptions.validation: Replace with quotes, measured branch mix, token and latency benchmarks.

Auto cap is 1000 minor units INR per incident; poor speed without a verified service breach and billing errors require supervisor review.

Account, service and billing adapters must offer authenticated tenant/subject reads, active connection version checks, scoped credit posting with a unique business-event key and definitive operation readback.

Proposed supervisor queue is staffed continuously, acknowledges cases within 1 elapsed hour, decides within 48 elapsed hours, and a duty manager owns overdue cases. Portal updates appear on entry and at 24 hours; overdue notice appears at 48 hours.
Proposed retention is 30 days for redacted model traces and 365 days for financial audit; deployment region, deletion exceptions and customer permissions need privacy review.
Illustrative traffic is 10000 cases/month; one explanation call per case, maximum two attempts. Assume 10% retry rate and 2000 input/300 output tokens at $1/$4 per million tokens.

sources.passage: Design a complaint assistant for a telecom provider. Customers report network outages, poor speed and billing errors. The assistant should investigate using account, billing and service records, explain findings and resolve eligible service credits. Larger or unclear refunds need a human supervisor and may wait up to 48 hours. Keep customers informed, avoid duplicate refunds and use only the right customer's active service connection. Propose any missing policies as assumptions, not real company rules.
